title: POC Weekly Sync - Quantization INT8/FP8
summary: Quick review of latest INT8/FP8 runs. FP8 shows small quality delta on long-context chat but higher memory saving not as large as expected; INT8 good for 99th percentile latency, FP8 better for throughput in some configs. Agreement to run 2k-sample QPT test, share updated perf/quality sheet, and run long-tail latency test in dedicated pool.
next_steps: Jordan to send updated perf/quality spreadsheet (by 2026-11-26)
Customer to run 2k-sample QPT with provided prompt set and share logs (by 2026-12-01)
Priya to schedule long-tail latency test on Dedicated pool (by 2026-11-30)
Jordan to include FP8 micro-batching config in baseline doc (by 2026-11-27)
Ravi to confirm test VPC access and instance types (by 2026-11-25)
action_items: Jordan Lee — send updated perf/quality spreadsheet with columns: model, quant, perf_50, perf_95, perf_99, quality_delta — due 2026-11-26
Priya Raman — run long-tail latency experiment on Dedicated pool (24h window) and upload traces — due 2026-11-30
Elena Martinez — run 2k-sample QPT test with INT8/FP8 configs and attach sample failures — due 2026-12-01
Ravi Kapoor — enable test VPC and confirm instance types (A10032/A30) — due 2026-11-25
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Okay good morning everyone, thanks for joining, this is the weekly quantization sync for Acme. We're at 45 minutes, agenda — quick status, go over the latest runs, and decide next steps.
[00:12] Elena Martinez: Morning all, we ran the FP8 experiments overnight, a couple of notes before we dive in.
[00:18] Priya Raman: Great, thanks Elena. Quick note, I'm on slightly delayed video so apologies if I interrupt.
[00:24] Tom Briggs: that's fine.
[00:27] Ravi Kapoor: Jumping in, just to say infra is ready for the dedicated pool tests once you confirm settings.
[00:33] Jordan Lee: Perfect, we'll cover that. OK Elena, can you summarise high level FP8 vs INT8?
[00:40] Elena Martinez: Sure. So we ran on the 13B baseline (the one you recommended) — native fp16 baseline, INT8 with symmetric quant, and an FP8 experimental build. The FP8 run reduced memory by about 18% relative to fp16, INT8 reduced by about 38% — so INT8 is still giving larger memory wins, surprise there was an expectation FP8 might be closer but results vary by operator mix.
[01:05] Maya Chen: And quality? we saw some small regressions?
[01:09] Elena Martinez: Right, on our QPT prompt set (500 sample quick pass) INT8 had an average Rouge-like quality delta of about -0.8% while FP8 was -0.4% — but the long-context chats, FP8 produced slightly fewer coherence drops.
[01:25] Jordan Lee: Hmm okay so INT8 is more aggressive but better memory. Priya, do you think the artifacts we saw are quantization noise or tokenization mismatch?
[01:33] Priya Raman: From the traces I saw it's mostly quant noise in some attention heads, the KV cache ops look a little lower precision in FP8 run, funny enough, the KV cache — sometimes transcribed as K V — is behaving differently. There's a couple attention heads that flip on longer sequences which causes hallucination-y fragments.
[01:52] Elena Martinez: We also saw timing out at 8k tokens for one run, that was likely a batching configuration mismatch — we had micro-batching turned off accidentally.
[02:00] Ravi Kapoor: On infra, we used A100-40 for the FP8 runs and A30 for INT8 tests to simulate production heterogeneity; maybe that's skewing results.
[02:09] Jordan Lee: Good point — we've been meaning to standardize that across runs. Let's note that as a confounder.
[02:15] Tom Briggs: Could that explain the smaller memory delta for FP8?
[02:18] Priya Raman: Partially, yes. Also compiler/kernels chosen differ by hardware. In the FP8 path we fell back to a less optimized kernel for some ops on A100-40's driver version; we can recompile or run on uniform hardware.
[02:33] Jordan Lee: Action item: uniform hardware for next comparative run.
[02:36] Elena Martinez: Agreed. Also, on latency: INT8 improved p50 by 18% and p95 by about 12%, but p99 improvement was modest, around 6%. FP8 gave p50 improvements of 10% but p95/p99 were slightly worse than INT8 in our snapshot.
[02:56] Maya Chen: That's interesting — it suggests INT8 is better for tail latency. For our use case tail matters a lot.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: Right, Acme's SLOs focus on 99th percentile for interactive chat.
[03:07] Ravi Kapoor: We need to make sure batching isn't hiding spikes. The micro-batch config and prefetch parameters changed between runs.
[03:13] Priya Raman: Yes, I noticed micro-batching set to 8 in the FP8 run vs 4 in INT8. That will push throughput and affect tails.
[03:20] Jordan Lee: Okay lets make the baseline explicit: same hardware, same micro-batching, same kernel set for the comparison.
[03:26] Tom Briggs: On quality samples — Elena, you mentioned hallucinations earlier. Any examples we can surface?
[03:30] Elena Martinez: Yeah I'll drop a couple transcripts in the sheet but one example: long contextual reference to a policy doc, INT8 truncated a clause and FP8 kept it but introduced a wrong date. It's subtle.
[03:43] Maya Chen: My read is FP8 reduces structural dropouts but introduces token-level noise in numeric entities.
[03:50] Priya Raman: That matches what I saw, numeric tokens are sensitive to FP8 exponent handling in some kernels.
[03:57] Jordan Lee: Noted. For next steps on quality, we proposed a 2k-sample QPT test — Elena and Maya can run that with both configs and include % of regressions by category (coherence, factual, numeric).
[04:10] Elena Martinez: Yes we can do that, will need the definitive prompt set and the scoring rubric.
[04:15] Jordan Lee: I'll send the QPT prompt pack and scoring rubric after the call.
[04:18] Priya Raman: On perf instrumentation, we'll enable tracing and upload flame traces; please make sure to include the p99 CPU wait metrics, sometimes the GPU is underutilized due to host stalls.
[04:31] Ravi Kapoor: For the dedicated tests, we can schedule a 24-hour long tail test to capture diurnal load and micro-bursts.
[04:38] Jordan Lee: Great. Priya, can you schedule?
[04:41] Priya Raman: Yep I'll schedule a 24-hour run on the dedicated pool and upload logs to the shared drive.
[04:46] Tom Briggs: Any security blockers for running dedicated?
[04:49] Ravi Kapoor: Not from our side, but we need the VPC peering details and a small firewall rule.
[04:54] Jordan Lee: Jordan: we'll send the VPC config doc and the Redwood private access checklist.
[04:58] Elena Martinez: Also can you add KMS integration notes? We want to make sure keys are customer-managed for logs.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include KMS/HSM notes and the audit log options.
[05:07] Maya Chen: A quick question — we talked about fallback policies earlier. If INT8 fails quality threshold, can we automatic fallback to FP16 or FP8?
[05:16] Priya Raman: Yes, Redwood runtime supports automated fallback to a pinned variant; we can configure thresholds (e.g. if perplexity delta > X or if quality regression > Y) and route to FP16. There's a small latency tax on fallback but it's fast.
[05:29] Tom Briggs: Good to know. That helps us meet SLOs.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: Competitor note: Acme had pilots with Bedrock and Triton; you mentioned Bedrock's managed endpoints were easy but cost was high — maybe list that in the sheet.
[05:42] Tom Briggs: yes we can.
[05:44] Elena Martinez: Back to results — small thing: we saw more tokenization mismatches in FP8 run for some domain-specific tokens (product SKUs). Might be a tokenizer edge-case.
[05:56] Maya Chen: We should include a tokenization test in the QPT suite then.
[05:59] Jordan Lee: Agreed. Put tokenization and numeric entity checks in the rubric.
[06:04] Ravi Kapoor: On infra, I'll confirm A100 availability and standardize the driver version across tests.
[06:10] Priya Raman: I'll re-run compilation with the updated kernel flags and share the exact git hash of the runtime.
[06:17] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Any blockers or final questions?
[06:20] Elena Martinez: No blockers, just need the prompt pack and perf sheet.
[06:24] Jordan Lee: We'll send those today. One more thing — can we plan a short demo of fallback in action next week? 10 minutes.
[06:32] Tom Briggs: Sure, schedule it.
[06:34] Jordan Lee: Cool. Recap of action items: Jordan to send perf sheet + prompt pack + KMS notes; Priya to schedule 24h dedicated run and compile; Elena/Maya to run 2k QPT; Ravi to confirm VPC and hardware. We'll meet same time next week. Thanks everyone.
[06:54] (end)
